curated.instructions: omr/instructions/42057-1-1.pdf (book 1 builds the helicopter, steps 1-86, the finished model on page 70); omr/instructions/42057-1-2.pdf builds the alternate model

functions.does: Turning the main rotor runs the three-cylinder engine behind the pilot: the rotor's mast turns the crankshaft through a pair of 12 tooth bevel gears, the three pistons pump up and down, and a 20 tooth gear on the crankshaft's back end turns the rear propeller's shaft through a 12 tooth gear, faster than the rotor.
functions.source: book: steps 31-36 (the crankshaft and pistons), 41-42 (the engine and its gears), 55-56 and 62 (the rotor mast, its bevel gear and the turning arrows), 72 (the propeller), 85-86 (the rotor); which part is meant to be turned by hand is inferred
functions.note: p113 is the rotor's mast; the rotor blades (p195, p196) sit on a long pin with a stop bush on top of it (steps 85-86), and the propeller p163 on the pin end of another (step 72), so it isn't certain the book means them to be held fast to their shafts

functions.does: The rear propeller turns with the engine and the main rotor.
functions.source: inferred: from the gears in steps 41-42 and the propeller fitted in step 72

functions.does: The red lever on the helicopter's right side, under the engine, swings the tail rudder: a steering link runs back from the lever's ball to a bellcrank (the beam with the 40 years print) under the engine, and a second steering link runs from the bellcrank to a ball on the rudder.
functions.source: book: steps 16-27 (the bellcrank, built as the tail control and fitted under the engine), 66-67 and 69 (the rudder on the tail), 71-72 (the lever and the link to it); that the lever works the rudder is inferred from the links

functions.does: The joystick in front of the pilot's seat tilts.
functions.source: inferred: the steering-wheel yoke on a cross block in the cockpit (steps 64-65); the book draws no link from it to anything
functions.note: unsure whether the joystick is meant to work the rudder too; in the book's steps it isn't linked to it

functions.does: The nose wheel and the two wheels on the red landing legs roll freely.
functions.source: book: step 4 (the nose wheel), steps 77 and 83 (the landing legs and their wheels)

questions.question: Are the rotor and propeller fixed to their shafts (they sit on pins)?
